newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK SHARES REGAIN FOOTING, OTE SLIPS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK SHARES REGAIN FOOTING, OTE SLIPS.

text.p: Greek shares came out of the cold and regained their footing, staying above 1,450 points in a 2.1 percent come-back after their recent 300-point slump.

The rebound, after a 50 percent retracement, came amid concerns over a stubborn CPI in the second half and firmer interbank rates. But current worries on the macro front were overdone, fund managers said.

"One should not miss the big picture -- the improvement in macroeconomic fundamentals which sparked an asset reallocation and drove the market to all-time highs has not reversed," said Alico Eurobank's chief investment officer Alex Pappas.
Growth funds were realising inflows against a background of falling prices, other fund managers said.
"Growth funds are witnessing an inflow of fresh funds despite the drop in equity prices, which indicates a more mature investment approach by retail investors," Karaboikis said.
Monday's second-biggest point loss on the Dow-Jones industrial average coupled with a drop in prices of US bonds did not impact Greek equities.
Market watchers pointed to a negative correlation in recent weeks with Greek stocks dipping against an international background of record-breaking performance.
The Athens general index closed 2.11 percent or 31.02 points higher at 1,498.94 from Monday's 1,467.92 close.
Turnover amounted to 16.4 billion drachmas on volume of 3.9 million shares.
Advancers led decliners 149 to 73 with 15 shares unchanged on 237 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted at London's SEAQ International market at $11.75-$12.05. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,110-1,140 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,163-1,223 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying instrument lost 100 drachmas to settle at 6,600.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 496.99-528.71 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $68.93-$70.62. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 2,841-3,050 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $11.16-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 191-221 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
